To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The cross section for the production of the $J/\psi$-meson in the reaction of a pion with the proton is 0.5 nb at 12 GeV.
the production of the bound states with hidden-charm, such as the $X$ and $Y$, can be studied at J-PARC, JLab and other facilities.

the production of hidden charm mesons in pion induced reactions is dominated by meson exchange and that the cross section for $\gamma^* N \rightarrow J/\Psi N$ is about a factor of two larger than the cross section for the production of the $P$-wave charmonium state $\chi_c$ in the same reaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of bound systems with hidden charm.
the production and decay of the $J/\psi$ meson in the nuclear environment.
the production of bound systems with hidden charm in the reactions induced by charged and neutral pions and real photons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the production of bound state with hidden charm is possible in the reactions induced by pion and photons.
the $J/\psi$ is not a good candidate for the $\Lambda_c^+$ and $\Lambda_c^-$ decays.
the production cross section of $\Lambda_{c}^{+}\Lambda_{c}^{-}$ is about 10 times higher at the $\pi^{+}$ beam energy of 6 GeV than at the $\gamma$ beam energy of 3.5 GeV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the cross-sections for the bound state production are large enough to be detected by the proposed experiments.
we are now in the position to perform a full calculation of the cross sections of the reactions $e^- p \to J/\Psi \, X$ at Jefferson Laboratory (JLab) and $p\pi^-\to J/\Psi\,X$ at J-PARC.

we have developed a model that is able to explain a large variety of experimental results on charmonium-like states and that can predict the production cross section for bound states with hidden heavy quarks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the production of hidden charm states is dominated by the production of the $J/\psi$ and the $J/\Phi$, with the production of the latter being suppressed by a factor of $1/3$.

, while there is no evidence for a bound state with hidden charm in pion-induced reactions, there are significant contributions to the total cross sections of the $J/\psi$ production from the formation of bound states in the photon-induced reactions.

the production of the $X(3872)$ and $X(3915)$ in the reactions $pp\rightarrow pK\pi X$ and $pp\rightarrow ppX$ is dominated by the $D\bar D^*$ and $J/\psi\pi\pi$ components, respectively, and the $X(3910)$ is produced dominantly in the $D\pi$ channel.
